summary: Takeo Kanaseki (1897–1983) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held posts at Kyushu University (~1949–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1969), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1969–1979).

Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi, then served at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987 as assistant to professor and professor emeritus (2021).

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post as lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and lecturer posts attested in 2026 at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Takeshi Karashima (1903–1967) was a sinologist who studied at Yamaguchi Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University (~1923–1926). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Kamakura's library (~1947–1949), Sagami Women's University, and Showa Women's University.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Nagoya University and under Tokuryu Yamauchi at Kyoto University. His posts included Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Takeshiro Kuraishi (1897–1975) was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949), held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and chaired Chugokugo Gakkai.

Takezo Kaneko (1905–1987) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1925–1928). He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1966) and International Christian University (~1966–1976), with additional posts at Seikei and Hokkaido universities.

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche (1926–2015) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He served as Supreme Head of the Nyingma tradition from around 2012 to 2015, succeeding Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö.

Taku Fukuda (born 1963) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He was appointed lecturer at Doho University in 1995 and was affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute as of 2026.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and held teaching appointments at Taisho University attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others. He served at Kanazawa University (~1974–2000), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (~2000).
Tamara Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed a PhD at the University of Toronto in 2023 under the doctoral supervision of Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.

Tampalawela Dhammaratana (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and conducted postdoctoral research at École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung (born 1929) is a historian and sinologist who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He held posts at the National Defence Academy, University of Delhi (~1964–1978), Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994), and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.
Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam.
Tan Sitong (1865–1898) was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wang Zhengyi (~1893–1898) and Renshan Yang (~1896–1898).

Tan Yun-shan (1898–1983) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Hunan Normal University and Chuanshan Academy, and with Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen. He taught at Lida Academy and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1968).
Tanaya Afroz is a linguistics scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a research scholar or fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.
Tandin Dorji is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He has held positions as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College and as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education, Paro.

Tanero Sasakawa (1870–1949) was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held posts at Meiji University (~1904–1930) and Toyo University.
